Reverse engineering

Firmware Emulation and Debugging

Planned notes on emulating firmware with QEMU, debugging with GDB, and comparing static analysis with observable behavior in embedded Linux.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series will investigate firmware emulation with QEMU and debugging with GDB. The work will connect static analysis with program execution, memory state, and the behavior of embedded Linux systems.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Emulation target and constraints

  • Choose a firmware image and a matching QEMU machine or board model.
  • Record missing peripherals and unsupported hardware blocks.
  • Define what the emulation is expected to prove.

Boot reconstruction

  • Load the kernel or bare-metal image at the correct address.
  • Provide required memory-mapped devices and boot arguments.
  • Capture the first successful console output.

Debugging with GDB

  • Attach GDB to the emulated target.
  • Set breakpoints on entry points and service handlers.
  • Inspect memory, registers, and stack state.

Static and dynamic comparison

  • Compare static findings with runtime behavior.
  • Trace configuration parsing and authentication paths.
  • Record differences caused by missing hardware.

Limits and references

  • State which conclusions depend on emulation fidelity.
  • Keep raw logs and command lines with the results.
  • Link QEMU and GDB documentation.

Topics to cover

  • QEMU firmware emulation
  • GDB debugging
  • Embedded Linux
  • Static and dynamic analysis
